saha: Rio Grande Gorge, Taos, New Mexico
baslik: Apollo 15 crew geology training at Rio Grande Gorge
metin: On 11–12 March 1971, Apollo 15 astronauts David Scott and James Irwin, with backup crew Richard Gordon and Harrison Schmitt, trained at the Rio Grande Gorge near Taos, New Mexico, the area that most closely resembled their Hadley–Apennine landing site. Driving the Grover rover simulator along the gorge rim, Scott and Irwin carried out a geologic investigation similar to the one they later made at Hadley Rille.

kaynak_belge: NASA ALSJ Ries trip 10–15 Aug 1970; Phinney, NASA SP-2015-626
baslik: Apollo 14 crew geology field trip to the Nördlinger Ries
metin: From 10 to 15 August 1970, Apollo 14 astronauts Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell, with backup crew Eugene Cernan and Joe Engle, made a geology field trip to the Nördlinger Ries impact crater in Germany. Their Fra Mauro landing site included the Cone Crater impact feature, so their training included impact sites on Earth.

baslik: Apollo 16 crew geology training at the Sudbury impact structure
metin: In July 1971, Apollo 16 astronauts John Young and Charles Duke explored the Sudbury Basin in Ontario, a meteorite impact structure long misinterpreted as volcanic in origin. A 2008 GSA abstract credits this training with helping them recognise the Cayley Formation at their landing site as impact breccia rather than volcanic rock.

baslik: Apollo 17 crew geology training at the Sudbury impact structure
metin: In 1972, a year after the Apollo 16 visit, Apollo 17 astronauts Harrison Schmitt and Gene Cernan trained in Sudbury, Ontario, for the final Moon landing. Because Schmitt was a trained geologist, their visit was run as a conventional geological tour rather than the mock lunar traverse used for Apollo 16.

baslik: JETT3 and JETT5 moonwalk simulations at SP Crater
metin: In October 2022, NASA's Joint EVA and Human Surface Mobility Test Team used the rocky terrain of SP Crater, north of Flagstaff, Arizona, as a lunar proxy for JETT3, a series of simulated moonwalks for the Artemis III EVA study. In May 2024, the JETT5 simulation returned to the San Francisco Volcanic Field, with landing sites mapped in the SP region.

baslik: Ephrata Fan as the Earth analog for the Mars Pathfinder landing site
metin: NASA scientists used the Ephrata Fan in the Channeled Scabland of Washington State as an Earth analog, together with orbital data, to predict the surface of the Mars Pathfinder landing site in Ares Vallis. Golombek et al. (1999) report that the surface and the largest clasts seen at the site were similar to the predictions based on the Ephrata Fan.

baslik: Curiosity mobility tests with Scarecrow at Dumont Dunes
metin: In May 2012, Mars Science Laboratory team members drove Scarecrow, a test rover with a full-scale copy of Curiosity's mobility system, up sandy slopes at Dumont Dunes in California's Mojave Desert. Data from its drives on windward and downwind dune slopes were to guide decisions on driving Curiosity on dunes near Mount Sharp in Gale Crater.

baslik: Apollo 15 crew geology training at Kilbourne Hole
metin: In January 1971, the Apollo 15 crew trained at Kilbourne Hole, a crater on public land in New Mexico. They collected volcanic samples along the crater's east rim and worked as if they were on the Moon.

saha: Rio Grande Gorge, Taos, New Mexico
baslik: Apollo 16 crew geology training at Rio Grande Gorge
metin: On 8–10 September 1971, Apollo 16 astronauts John Young and Charles Duke, with backup crew Fred Haise and Edgar Mitchell, made a geology field trip to the Rio Grande Gorge near Taos, New Mexico. On this trip they used Grover, the geologic rover built by the U.S. Geological Survey, for the first time.

baslik: Apollo 17 crew practice EVA in the Lunar Crater Volcanic Field
metin: In September 1972, Apollo 17 astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt carried out a practice EVA in the Lunar Crater Volcanic Field near Tonopah, Nevada, as part of their science training (Phinney, NASA SP-2015-626).

baslik: JETT1 field test near Kilbourne Hole
metin: In 2022, NASA's Joint EVA Test Team held its first field test, JETT1, near Kilbourne Hole by El Paso, Texas, at a site chosen for its relevance to the expected Artemis lunar terrain. The test focused on hardware development and checkout and was the first field deployment of the ExCon mockup spacesuit.
